On-chain, all that remains is a single, cold interception error. This kind of “dimensionality reduction strike,” which tightly seals the security checkpoint at the front end, really does flip the long-standing crypto-currency circle script of “lose the coins first, then try to seek redress, only to get treated like a joke.”

#newt $NEWT Deep experience over nearly a month—spending every day immersed in Newton Protocol’s cross-chain pools and intent trading, and I guess I’ve finally seen through the cards. Don’t believe the outside hype about “AI + Web3.” In essence, it’s an extremely precise on-chain meat grinder.

First, let’s talk about staking. Earning yield by taking $NEWT  sounds good, but the mandatory unlock period of half a month is unbearable. When the market turns, you can only stare blankly. This rule weeds out short-term traders and stabilizes the core base, but for retail users it’s effectively exploitation. No matter how much capital you have, you wait the same amount of time—purely making small retail traders stand guard on network consensus to “hold the fort” for free.

Next, automated trading. Cross-chain running of strategies is pretty smooth. I’ve even quietly profited from some obscure spreads before. But once the arbitrage route gets exposed, it immediately turns into a red ocean. Everyone on the internet surges in at once—extreme gas fees and slippage instantly wipe out profits. Sometimes the money you make in a session isn’t even enough to cover the $NEWT  transaction fees. There’s no safety net here. Opportunities that retail traders dig out at 2 a.m. can be effortlessly snatched away by giant whales with raw compute power.

As for on-chain agents, that’s even deeper water. To run models, you first need to stake tokens, but the entry threshold for advanced robots is sky-high—ordinary players can’t reach it. And there’s basically no smooth channel in the ecosystem to transfer strategies. The code you painstakingly debug becomes public and outdated pretty quickly, and if you can’t sell it, you’re stuck eating the loss yourself.

Put plainly, Newton Protocol turns users into “digital hostages” by locking up liquidity. It extracts arbitrage space by leveraging agents, forcefully binding demand tightly to the ecosystem. Instead of spending every day in the secondary market watching token prices and gambling on up or down, you’d be better off steadily studying the system and using real on-chain work to earn your way to the chips—the real solution. @NewtonProtocol #eth

title: 沦为废铁的权限与暗改的门槛：Newton链上那台吃人不吐骨头的榨汁机
subTitle:
东京的夜色快褪干净了，这间涩谷的单身公寓里冷清得可怕，只有马路对面的霓虹灯还在闪。盯着屏幕上第三次弹出的红叉，我那杯放了一宿的挂耳早就喝不出味了。前些天，听说Newton打算放开节点限额，我卯足了劲去肝Kaito的活跃度，盘算着把手头的NEWT全扔进那个肥得流油的池子。结果呢？大门一开，网页上标的底价全特么是障眼法！链上实际执行的起步线足足高了25%。海量资金一窝蜂涌进Keystore Rollup，把通道挤得跟春运的火车站一样。我硬着头皮连发三笔交易，两笔直接被节点踢回来，另一笔在链上足足卡了四十分钟。手续费烧得人心疼不说，等好不容易挤进去，肉早被别人吃光了。
这绝对不是网页没刷新的问题。事后我去扒了那几天的区块记录，才发现注册合约里暗搓搓地埋了一根“弹簧”。只要押进去的总量摸到某根红线，进场费就自动往上抬。白皮书里对这个动态调节机制装聋作哑，但小圈子里早就有人摸清了门道。那些老油条的地址，每次都能精准卡在门槛跳涨前的一眨眼功夫落袋为安。你以为是人家网速快？那是赤裸裸的降维收割，玩的是信息不对称。@NewtonProtocol #ETH 
再掰扯掰扯他们引以为傲的那个意图网络。过去这半年，我试过无数套自动化指令，从无脑挂单到跨链套利。Newton官方管这叫“模块化代理”，吹得天花乱坠，仿佛给了散户一把屠龙刀。可我拿真金白银滚出来的结论是：这套玩意儿根本没降低什么操作门槛，唯一的用处就是拼车图便宜。把一堆意图打包凑一车，单笔的Gas费确实能省下一半。#newt $NEWT 
但这省下来的几块钱，全在权限的贬值里亏了个底朝天。早前我花高价在二手市场收了几个跟风策略的NFT，本指望能捂热了赚差价。结果没过两周，项目方反手就把底层代码给全网公开了。短短三天，同款代理烂大街，我手里这批权限的底价直接跌穿了发行成本。更让人吐血的是，这些代理的命脉全攥在协议版本手里。Newton只要稍微改改执行环境，旧版代理瞬间报废。上链确权听着高大上，但你确权的是一张已经进不了站的废票。节点套牢的是你的本金，而代理耗尽的是版本的寿命。
顺着这套逻辑往下挖，质押系统的阶层歧视更是让人恶心。我特意拿自己重度交互的老号和新注册的白板号做了个测试：同样是申请全节点，老号在底层逻辑里直接自带VIP加权，而新号连去普通池子里喝口汤的资格都没有。这根本不是什么运气成分，而是合约里早就写死的等级制度。你以前的活跃天数、打包交易的次数，甚至Kaito的评分，全被折算成了隐形的优先权。官方冠冕堂皇地说是为了防女巫攻击，说穿了这就是在链上搞三六九等。
大户们舒舒服服地躺在核心位置收租，散户只能在底层池子里捡残渣，而那漫长的两周锁定期更是杀人不见血。我之前有一笔普通质押好不容易熬到头，偏偏赶上大盘泥沙俱下。那整整十四天，我只能眼睁睁看着NEWT的价格断崖式暴跌，却什么操作都做不了。等到终于能把币提出来，账面直接蒸发了将近两成。这哪是什么正常的波动风险？这根本就是项目方精心设计的“断头台”——你的资产在最危险的时候被牢牢锁死，而协议的金库却能毫发无损地抽着流水提成。
至于NEWT的盘面走势，我看透了里面的套路。盘点了最近两个月的链上动静，基本就是个明牌的剧本：只要席位一扩招，或者来一波集中结算，代币的转账量就立马飙升个三四成，价格也跟着往上窜一窜。可一旦这阵风刮过去，抛压比谁都狠，跌回去的幅度往往更深。再看他们那个忽悠人的销毁逻辑——号称手续费全用来通缩，但实际上只要扩招间隔超过半个月，烧掉的那点份额在天量通胀面前连个零头都算不上。这种所谓的通缩叙事，简直就像拿个小水瓢去舀太平洋，自欺欺人。
按照这帮人的行事作风，Newton下一步铁定会对质押的节奏动刀子，盯着市场上的流通盘和代理饱和度来玩控盘。说不定哪天又搞出个旧代理“合成升级”的噱头，随便画个饼来安抚一下手里捏着废票的散户。当然，这些都是基于合约逻辑的猜测，毕竟人家的官方路线图上现在还在装死呢。
说到底，Keystore Rollup这套底层框架确实有点技术含量，但它骨子里就是一个吃人不吐骨头的过滤网：用隐形的门槛把小散挡在门外，用锁定期把资金关门打狗，再用高频的更新把老资产洗劫一空。刚入圈的新手，千万别被高收益迷了眼直接冲进去，拿点小钱熟悉熟悉怎么付Gas、怎么排队才是正经事。老玩家也别一棵树上吊死，学会把资金拆开，尽量错开那些扎堆开放和解锁的高峰期。在这地方玩，光凭胆子大没用，得看懂那些没写在网页上的代码猫腻。天大亮了，手边的残渣也该倒了，继续查当天的队列深度去吧。

translatedData.title: Reduced to Scrap Metal: The Permissions and Hidden Changes Behind Newton’s On-Chain Barriers
translatedData.subTitle: The night in Tokyo is almost gone now. This lonely single apartment in Shibuya is terrifyingly quiet—only the neon lights across the street are still flickering. Staring at the red X that’s popped up on my screen for the third time, the single-serve pour-over that I left steeping all night no longer tastes like anything. A few days ago, I heard Newton was planning to loosen the node quota limits. I threw everything I had into grinding Kaito’s activity, thinking I’d dump all my NEWT into that fat, oozing pool. So what happened? The moment the door opened, the “base price” shown on the website was nothing but smoke and mirrors. The actual on-chain starting line was a full 25% higher. Massive money poured into the Keystore Rollup all at once, squeezing the channels until it felt like the train station during Chunyun. I forced myself to send three transactions—two were rejected by the nodes outright, and the other one stalled on-chain for a full forty minutes. Not only did the gas fees burn my heart to pieces, but by the time I finally squeezed in, the meat was already gone, devoured by someone else.

translatedData.content:
Is MoneyGram joining Solana a major positive development or a hidden risk? The real thing to worry about is this!
MoneyGram has officially started running Solana validating nodes, which means traditional financial institutions are accelerating their entry into the Solana ecosystem—a significant milestone for the entire network.
However, institutional involvement also brings new issues. To meet regulatory and fund-safety requirements, these large organizations are unlikely to be fully open like ordinary nodes; instead, they are more likely to set up transaction flows and validation mechanisms that comply with regulatory rules.
While this can improve security and make it easier to attract traditional financial capital, it may also result in more and more large amounts of money flowing only through a limited number of “compliant channels.”
If, in the future, more and more institutions adopt this model, Solana may receive more funding but could also see liquidity gradually become concentrated, weakening the original open, decentralized characteristics.
So, this is both an opportunity and a test. Institutional capital can drive ecosystem growth, but finding the right balance between compliance and decentralization is the key factor that truly determines Solana’s long-term value. $SOL $BLUAI $POWER #ETH

content:
MoneyGram加入Solana，是大利好还是隐藏风险？真正值得担心的是这一点！
MoneyGram已经正式运行Solana验证节点，这意味着传统金融机构正在加速进入Solana生态，对整个网络来说无疑是一个重要进展。
不过，机构进场也带来了新的问题。为了满足监管和资金安全要求，这些大型机构不会像普通节点一样完全开放，而是更倾向于建立符合监管规则的交易流程和验证机制。
这样做虽然能提高安全性，也更容易吸引传统金融资金进入，但也可能让越来越多的大额资金只在少数“合规通道”中流动。
如果未来越来越多机构都采用这种模式，Solana虽然会迎来更多资金，却也可能让流动性逐渐集中，削弱原本开放、去中心化的特点。
所以，这件事既是机会，也是考验。机构资金能够推动生态发展，但如何在合规和去中心化之间找到平衡，才是真正决定Solana长期价值的关键。 $SOL $BLUAI $POWER #ETH

大户吃肉，小散户连残羹冷炙都摸不着，而那个长达两周的强制冷静期更是杀人诛心。我之前一笔普通质押好不容易熬到头，偏偏撞上大盘一波连环爆跌。那14天里，只能眼睁睁看着NEWT的价格一泻千里却动弹不得。等到终于能解套走人，账面上直接缩水了百分之二十。这根本不是正常波动的锅，而是项目方给你上的“枷锁税”——你的资产在最危急的关头被死死锁进黑洞，而协议的资金库却能雷打不动地抽着流水提成。
至于NEWT的盘面走势，完全被摸透了底牌。我盘点了一下近两个月的数据，基本是按着剧本在走：只要官方搞个名额扩招，或者来一波集中意图结算，NEWT的链上转账量就立马飙升三四成，币价也顺势往上窜一窜。可一旦热度冷却，抛压比谁都狠，跌幅绝对盖过涨幅。再看看他们那套自欺欺人的销毁逻辑——号称手续费全用来通缩，但实际上只要扩招间隔超过两星期，烧掉的那点币在庞大的通胀面前连塞牙缝都不够。这种通缩故事，简直像往太平洋里滴了一滴墨水，闹着玩呢。
照这个吃相，Newton下一步大概率会拿质押的节奏开刀，盯着市场上的流通盘和代理饱和度来玩饥饿营销。保不齐哪天又搞个废旧代理“合成进化”的花活儿，好安抚一下手里捏着一堆废票的怨种散户。当然，这些纯属看透合约逻辑后的瞎猜，人家官方可是静悄悄装死呢。
扯了这么多，说句实在话，Keystore Rollup这套底层框架确实有点干货。但这套机制骨子里就是一个榨汁机：用隐形门槛把小散挡在门外，用锁定期把流动性关门打狗，再用频繁更新把老资产洗劫一空。刚入局的菜鸟，千万别上头去冲高收益池，拿点零花钱熟悉熟悉Gas怎么扣、队列怎么排才是正经事。老油条们也别搞单吊，学会分仓操作，把锁定期尽量错开。在这地方混，信直觉不如去读懂那些没写在网页上的代码猫腻。天亮了，手边那杯浑水也被我倒了，接着盯盘去了。

translatedData.subTitle: The night in Tokyo’s Shibuya had dragged on until it was almost over; I slumped in my cramped ten-some-square-meter rental, and through the window I could just make out the glowing fluorescent sign of a Lawson downstairs. On my screen, my little Fox wallet had reported errors for the third time in a row: “Reverted.” The cold brew I’d left on the table, untouched, had gone ice-cold. Not long ago I heard Newton was going to expand its node-name quota, so I started grinding activity on Kaito a full week early, thinking the NEWT I had in my pocket would be enough to buy me a high-yield slot. Who would’ve thought that the instant the threshold opened, the so-called benchmark shown in the web front-end was just playing dumb—on-chain contract deductions were actually over twenty percent higher than the number the interface displayed. A huge wave of funds poured into Keystore Rollup in the same second, clogging the channels tight as a drum. I forced myself through three times: twice got bounced back, and once I just spun in place for almost half an hour. It was all for nothing—not only did I burn a pretty penny on fees, but when I finally got in, the good stuff—the pickings—was already gone.

#newt  There’s been a lot of buzz lately about Newton (Newton Mainnet Beta) on-chain governance. I’m not the type to blindly follow the trend and talk nonsense—I've personally cast three votes with $NEWT , and I dug through Chapter 20 of the whitepaper thoroughly. To be honest, a lot of DAOs in the crypto space are really kind of flimsy: you can randomly mess with the treasury without any real barriers. Compared with that, Newton’s mechanism is much more solid. No stake, no right to speak—so it directly filters out short-term free-riders. Also, in the Beta stage, both the use of funds and changes to penalty parameters are reviewed with multi-signature oversight by the foundation. Proposal deposits are automatically returned by smart contracts—no human backroom manipulation. That part really is reassuring.

@NewtonProtocol 

But if you dig deeper into the voting records, there’s a major flaw that’s easy for retail users to fall into: it looks only at the amount of voting power, not the holding period. Chapter 20 doesn’t grant any special weighting to players who lock tokens for the long term. That means if a whale pulls in capital for a short-term push and floods the system, in minutes they can steer the direction of proposals. And then all of us who stubbornly hold our chips get marginalized instead. Even more awkward: delegation voting hasn’t been enabled yet. With limited time and energy, small holders can’t realistically keep up—so the threshold for true community governance is actually pretty high.

Let’s imagine an extreme dump scenario: when the market crashes hard, the hot money rushes in and shorts/stakes $NEWT for the short term, seizing the opportunity to push for lowering fines for node violations. Retail voters’ stakes are too scattered to stop this kind of move. Once they succeed, the cost for malicious behavior by nodes drops significantly, and the network will likely run into problems frequently. And by the time you realize it and want to fix it? They can immediately flip around and collectively vote “no,” and the whole system can basically freeze.

From the lessons I’ve picked up after years of being around on-chain, I want to advise everyone with $NEWT : don’t be tempted by a little bit of interest and hand your tokens over casually. If you’re really planning to run with the ecosystem long-term, set aside a baseline position specifically for staking. If you have time, also take a look or two at upcoming motions before they go live—study the rules in Chapter 20 and then exercise your voting power. Don’t end up being the sacrifice of big capital that’s just playing with the rulebook.#eth $ETH

In contrast, the transition period setup in Newton’s whitepaper, Chapter 20, is much more solid. Under this rule, if you want to initiate a motion or participate in voting, you must stake NEWT—this directly filters out opportunistic speculators who try to “fast-forward.” Also, for core motions like treasury fund requests and adjustments to node penalty ratios, the Beta period adds a foundation multisig for pre-checks specifically. Previously, I tried to submit a motion to modify the challenge period. Even though it didn’t pass, the staked coins were automatically fully returned by the smart contract, with no manual intervention throughout the process. The logic is far more rigorous than those chaotic ecosystems.

However, after reviewing the historical vote counts, I also found hidden landmines. This system currently only recognizes the amount of coins, and it doesn’t care how long you’ve held them. Chapter 20 doesn’t design weighted multipliers for long-term stakers. That means once large opportunistic funds rush in short-term with massive stakes, it becomes easy to dominate the盘. On top of that, proxy voting hasn’t been opened. Ordinary retail users who don’t constantly monitor the market basically can’t get a hand in. Let’s consider an extreme market crash scenario: when the broader market is in bad shape, speculative capital comes in to short-term stake NEWT and forms a group to push for reducing the penalties for nodes committing wrongdoing. Since the die-hard supporters’ stakes are too fragmented, these malicious proposals are likely to pass. Once they do, the cost for nodes to do bad things drops significantly, and on-chain errors are bound to become frequent. And when you later want to patch the vulnerabilities, these short-term big holders would collectively vote “no” again—causing the entire network governance to fall into paralysis.

Based on my experience of stepping on these kinds of pitfalls over the years, here’s some advice for the old-timers holding $NEWT : don’t mindlessly custody your coins for the small, immediate gains in front of you. translatedData.content:
A small pitfall in Newton documentation is deadly: expireAfter cannot be set to 0; otherwise the attestation will expire immediately upon birth
In Newton smart contract integration documentation, there’s a particularly practical pitfall: expireAfter cannot be set to 0.#ETH 
This parameter looks like just a small field in the policy configuration, but it determines how long an attestation can live. Newton’s on-chain verification doesn’t only check whether the “operator has agreed”—it also checks whether this attestation has expired. In NewtonPolicyClient, it performs this check:
block.number < attestation.expiration
So the proof isn’t a permanent pass. It’s only valid within a specific block window.
The documentation directly warns: if expireAfter == 0, NewtonPolicyData.initialize() will revert with InvalidExpireAfter(). The reason is simple: 0 makes the attestation’s expiration == reference_block. By the time the user’s transaction is actually sent to the chain and gets included, the current block already satisfies block.number >= expiration, so verification immediately turns into AttestationExpired.
In plain terms: you obtain a freshly generated approval result, but it has already become invalid before the transaction is mined and included.#BTC 
This detail really shows Newton’s design focus. It’s not just about generating a “passed” result and being done; it constrains that result to a specific time window. If the window is too short, users won’t have time to execute; if it’s too long, the risk of old proofs being misused increases. That’s why the official docs recommend using at least 150 blocks on the testnet—roughly a 5-minute-level window on Base.
I think this is more interesting than the vague claim that “on-chain authorization is safer.” Real fund security often doesn’t die in grand narratives—it dies in these tiny edge cases: when a proof is generated, when it can still be used, and when it must be invalidated.
Newton turns the attestation into an object that expires, gets verified, and is meant for single use. This indicates it’s not just making a “just let it through” signature button—it’s converting off-chain judgment into an on-chain-controlled execution credential.
#Newt  $NEWT @NewtonProtocol

content:
Newton 文档里这个小坑很致命：expireAfter 不能设成 0，否则 attestation 一出生就过期
Newton 智能合约集成文档里一个特别实在的坑：expireAfter 不能设成 0。#ETH 
这个参数看起来只是 policy 配置里的一个小字段，但它决定 attestation 能活多久。Newton 的链上验证不是只看“operator 有没有同意”，还要看这份 attestation 有没有过期。NewtonPolicyClient 里会检查：
block.number < attestation.expiration
也就是说，证明不是永久通行条。它只在一个区块窗口里有效。
文档里直接提醒：如果 expireAfter == 0，NewtonPolicyData.initialize() 会报 InvalidExpireAfter()。原因很简单，0 会让 attestation 的 expiration == reference_block。等用户把交易发到链上、交易真正被打包时，当前区块已经满足 block.number >= expiration，于是验证直接变成 AttestationExpired。
翻成人话就是：你拿到了一份刚生成的批准结果，但它在交易被矿工打包前就已经失效了。#BTC 
这个细节挺能说明 Newton 的设计重心。它不是只生成一份“通过”的结果就完事，而是把这份结果限定在具体时间窗口里。窗口太短，用户来不及执行；窗口太长，旧证明被滥用的风险变大。所以官方文档建议测试网至少用 150 个区块，大约是 Base 上 5 分钟级别的窗口。
我觉得这比泛泛说“链上授权更安全”有意思。真正的资金安全经常不是死在宏大叙事，而是死在这种很小的边界条件：证明什么时候生成，什么时候还能用，什么时候必须作废。
Newton 把 attestation 做成会过期、会校验、会被单次使用的对象，说明它不是在做一个随便放行的签名按钮，而是在把链下判断变成链上可控的执行凭证。
#Newt  $NEWT @NewtonProtocol

title: 屏蔽市场噪音：实盘跑通Newton节点，聊聊没有防火墙的残酷博弈
subTitle:
最近同行们都在疯炒Newton Mainnet Beta节点的收益率，但我这人天生反骨，越热的盘子越要冷眼看。这段时间我基本断网，成天泡在链上扒数据底稿，拿着白皮书第十九章的条款逐字倒推，连带着自己开测试机跑了好几圈。现在的项目方套路深，作恶成本极低，最后全是我们这些出资人当韭菜。我做投研的规矩没变：只认自己挖出来的链上铁证。今天就干脆把实测的底牌亮一亮。
讲句公道话，亲自把全套流程跑通后，Newton这套防作弊系统在当下的环境里确实能打。我手头的NEWT是拆开打散放的，每天的功课就是查预言机和签名回执。这套玩法最得我心的地方在于绝对的“去信任化”。不管你是多大的机构，哪怕是基金会，只要节点敢改数据或者掉链子，智能合约直接按死，哈希上链留底。没有任何人工扯皮的余地。
按照他们设定的规矩，咱们手握筹码的人只要在特定区块时间窗里把符合要求的ZK证明交上去，立马就能启动仲裁。我实盘跑的时候，正巧撞见两次节点数据同步出问题。单子一提交，去冲杯咖啡的功夫，系统就把判定做完了。违规方的抵押款被干脆利落地划扣，我也顺顺当当领到了挑战者的奖金。这种不废话的机器判决，才是撑起主网Beta庞大DeFi风控流转的核心基石。
但做了这么多年风控，我深知阳光越刺眼，背后的阴影越深。把第十九章掰碎了揉烂了看，最大的软肋就在于“一损俱损”。现在市面上很多包工头节点，拿着大家质押的同一批$NEWT，左手做AI数据校验，右手去接DeFi金库的活。最要命的是，这中间没有任何防火墙隔离！一旦他在某个冷门业务上踩了雷，整个质押底仓直接被连锅端。我们散户的本金莫名其妙就成了节点试错的炮灰。
再聊聊官方那个“全员可监督”的噱头，听着很美好，实操起来极其扯淡。弄出一个能让链上认可的ZK零知识证明，你得有硬核的本地运算设备，还要有徒手撕底层代码的能力。试问有哪个买币的老铁会去搞这种极其硬核的技术基建？日子一长，这个圈子的裁判权自然而然就落到了那些装备精良的超级大户手里。普通持币者看起来有尚方宝剑，其实连剑匣子都打不开。@NewtonProtocol 
此外，我极度警惕极端暴跌下的连环踩踏。万一大盘崩盘，所有人第一反应肯定是解绑NEWT套现保平安。可规则里卡着个14天的提现冷静期，这等于是把大家的逃生通道给锁死了。这种时候，如果碰上黑心大节点恶意串通改预言机，散户既拿不出ZK证明去反击，又没法割肉离场。等那套繁琐的机器罚没程序走完，咱们账面缩水的幅度，绝对比节点交的那点罚金惨烈百倍。$NEWT 
顺着往下盘，还有一个细思极恐的死局。万一排名前几的巨头节点哪天达成了默契，一起做假账，普通散户去举证的Gas磨损和算力开销，很可能会比你拿到的奖金还要贵。只要账面上是亏本买卖，谁还会去当这个吹哨人？当维权变成做慈善，这套花里胡哨的制衡体系在商业逻辑上就不攻自破了。#newt 
综合这段时间的摸底，我给拿着 #Newt 的散户交个底。
坚决切碎仓位： 绝对不能重仓押注在单一平台，一定要把委托额度拆开，防备那种连带式的爆仓。
别贪巨头高息： 看见那些收益极高的机构节点绕着走，别被眼前的利润蒙了心，权限大意味着隐患大。
握紧原始凭据： 平时自己长点心，定期存一存交互的凭证底稿，别把家当全抛给别人就不管了。
Newton这套东西好坏都明摆着，之后我依然会死盯主网Beta的参数改动，见机行事。在这个市场里，能熬到最后的才是赢家。#eth $ETH

Recently, my peers have been wildly speculating on the returns of Newton Mainnet Beta nodes, but I’m naturally contrarian—I look coldly at whatever is hottest. During this time, I’ve basically been offline, spending all day digging through on-chain data working papers, and methodically reconstructing everything word-for-word using the provisions in Chapter 19 of the whitepaper. I even set up my own test machines and ran them through several rounds. Now, the project team’s playbook is deep and the cost of wrongdoing is extremely low; in the end, it’s always we funders who get treated like the “grass” in a yield-harvesting cycle. My rules for investment research haven’t changed: I only recognize the on-chain ironclad evidence I dig up myself. So today, I’ll just lay out the tested trump card.
Speak fair words, and after personally running the entire end-to-end process, I can say that Newton’s anti-cheating system really does perform in today’s environment. The NEWT I have on hand was dismantled and scattered for testing; my daily homework is checking the oracle and the signed receipt. What I like most about this gameplay is its absolute “de-trust.” No matter how big the institution is—even a foundation—as long as a node dares to alter the data or drops the ball, the smart contract simply shuts it down, and the hash is anchored on-chain for audit trails. There’s no room for any human back-and-forth.

title: 链上实盘揭秘：扒一扒Newton节点质押的真金白银与隐性深坑
subTitle:
这段时间社群里关于Newton Mainnet Beta节点质押的讨论热度极高，但绝大多数人纯粹是冲着高年化去的，没几个人愿意花精力去啃枯燥的底层代码。做投研这么多年，我不信宣发只信数据。这大半个月我推掉其他事，直接扎进链上查验原始记录，把白皮书第十九章的规则一字一句拆开看，自己也搭环境跑了实测。市面上那种惩罚规则形同虚设、散户单方面扛亏损的盘子我见多了，今天纯粹从我个人的硬核复盘角度，给大家交个实底。
真刀真枪跑下来，Newton这套白皮书第十九章的框架，在当前的公链大环境里确实算得上是一股清流。我的NEWT底仓是分批委托的，每天的必修课就是去核对签名和预言机数据。这项目最讨喜的地方在于绝对的“自动化裁决”：没有什么所谓的基金会介入或者人工审核，一切判定、扣款、发奖全看智能合约的脸色。只要运营商敢作弊或者掉线，哈希记录直接锁死证据，这种透明度确实让人踏实。
按照他们的设定，持币者只要在限制的区块高度内把合规的ZK证明交上去，就能直接在链上硬刚作恶节点。我自己在测试节点时，正好逮到了两次延迟提交的违规动作。把申诉发上链后，一顿饭的功夫结果就出来了，对方被按比例强制扣除筹码，我也顺利拿到了拨付的挑战赏金。正因为有这种不讲人情的清算速度，主网Beta才能稳稳兜住现在庞大的DeFi交易量。@NewtonProtocol 
但这套逻辑是不是真就完美无缺？深扒细则之后，我发现里面的暗坑不小。打个比方，这就好比你给商铺交了押金，规矩定得很严，但防火墙没建好。我查链上数据时注意到，一大批运营商在用同一批质押的$NEWT，同时接着AI校验和DeFi风控好几个活儿。要命的是这里根本没有分仓隔离机制，只要某一条线出了岔子，质押池子直接被“一锅端”。这等于咱们散户的钱在替所有业务的风险买单，而大部分人对这种连带受罚的机制毫无察觉。$NEWT 
官方宣传语里一直强调“人人皆可挑战”，但这句口号在现实中非常苍白。懂点技术的朋友都知道，跑出一个有效的ZK零知识证明，对设备算力和底层数据解析能力的要求有多离谱。指望普通买币的人天天挂着高配服务器去维权？根本不现实。长此以往，链上的监督大权注定只会掉进那几个设备齐全的头部机构口袋里。散户名义上有权，实际上连门槛都跨不过去。#newt 
另外，作为老手，我本能地会对极端暴跌行情做压力测试。一旦市场出现大级别的跳水，恐慌盘必然排队解锁NEWT套现。但协议里那14天的冷静期，会像铁笼一样把流动性彻底锁死。如果在这个时候，某些大节点趁乱在预言机上动手脚，咱们普通人既搞不出ZK证明去反击，又没法立刻撤资走人。等到漫长的合约流程跑完，账面上的缩水幅度，绝对远超那点微薄的违规罚金。
顺着这个思路再往下推演一步：如果哪天几家头部大节点暗中联手作假，普通用户去发起申诉的Gas费和算力成本，极有可能发生倒挂，甚至比拿到的赏金还要高。一旦维权变成了一件倒贴钱的差事，这套看似无懈可击的制衡逻辑，在经济学层面就直接破产了，没人会去干这种费力不讨好的活。
结合我这段时间摸爬滚打的经验，给持有 #Newt 的兄弟们提三个醒：
一切忌单吊： 筹码必须分散委托给多个不同类型的节点，彻底切断连带爆仓的隐患。
二别迷信大户： 别看见那些机构节点给的年化高就无脑冲，权限越大，背后的系统性风险往往也越高。
三勤做备份： 养成定期下载链上交互回执的习惯，别真把币一锁就当甩手掌柜。
目前Newton的经济模型长板和短板都摆在台面上，后面我会继续死磕主网Beta的治理更新，随时调整仓位。在这个圈子，活下来永远比赚一时的快钱重要。#eth $ETH

subTitle:
凌晨翻阅 Newton Protocol 白皮书第11段，只要你稍懂点行，就会被那句“待后量子技术就绪后”给死死卡住。官方在这里玩了个极高的文字游戏，把概率事件硬说成了时间问题。他们描绘了一个无比丝滑的未来：一旦时机成熟，底层的 X25519 和 BLS 就能原地平移到 ML-KEM 与 ML-DSA，甚至宣称这只是一次“常规参数修改”。说穿了，这根本不是什么扎实的工程规划，而是一种洗脑。它要求你闭上眼睛祈祷，去赌那台能破解一切的超级机器，绝对不会在协议彻底竣工前问世。
官方文件里大肆鼓吹基于 HPKE 打造的隐私层，把“支持组件热更新”吹上了天。这其实是一记极其恶劣的障眼法。他们用代码结构上的“好维护”，去偷换了系统当下的“抗打击能力”，借此糊弄市场上那些合理的质疑声。你此刻上传并自以为私密的那些信息，实打实全被传统的椭圆曲线算法包裹着。面对未来算力暴涨的机器，这种防御层连纸糊的都不如。项目方的潜台词再明显不过：咱们以后肯定会建坚固的堡垒，但现在，你得先在帐篷里忍着。@NewtonProtocol 
咱们得正视这背后的算力碾压。现有的非对称加密，老底全扎在离散对数这个数学难题上。一旦有人把 Shor 算法塞进容错率达标的量子设备里，这道防线瞬间就会土崩瓦解。即便 NIST 刚把 ML-KEM 这些新方案盖了戳，但那都是没经过岁月毒打的雏儿。学术圈那帮人天天盯着这些新方向找岔子，之前名噪一时的 Rainbow 签名方案就是前车之鉴，没撑过两天就被个人电脑给干碎了。格密码怎么调参才兼顾性能和防御，至今还没个准信，这绝对不是一顿随时能上桌的快餐。
就算从代码仓库的角度看，挂载一个新加密包确实不难。但把这种操作等同于“无痛过渡”，纯属自欺欺人。底层更换验证机制，意味着全网所有参与者的旧身份凭证通通报废。因为新老两套密码学逻辑水火不容，大家必须重新生成私钥，曾经存下来的所有加密历史记录都得翻出来重做，节点池还得推倒重来一遍分布式密钥的生成流程。如果 Newton 真的做到了百万日活，这哪是什么后台改个参数？这分明是强迫上百万号人同时去办一张全新的赛博身份证，稍有不慎就是大规模的数据断层。$NEWT 
整个迁移计划里最让人头皮发麻的，是官方避而不谈的“阵痛期”。在这个不可避免的过渡阶段，系统必须硬抗着同时解析旧版和新版的加密流。安全圈的人都清楚，这种拼接状态简直就是漏洞温床。只要其中一套机制存在缝隙，整体的安全阀门就会被直接撬开。参考之前 OpenSSH 爆出的降级漏洞就懂了，攻击者完全能利用这种新老交替的混乱，强行剥离掉你的新防护，逼你退回到最弱的那个版本去通信。Newton 引以为豪的模块化，在这种时候反而成了到处漏风的筛子。
这种掩耳盗铃的做法，其实是在给 $NEWT 的共识机制埋雷。设想一个场景：某天科技巨头突然发个公告，宣布他们用几百个逻辑量子比特跑通了核心算法的缩水版。只要这层技术窗户纸一捅破，整个金融和链圈的信仰体系就会瞬间崩塌。到那时候，没人会管你白皮书里写了多完美的迁移路线，全网只会陷入疯狂的避险踩踏。而 Newton 最大的卖点——去中心化，此时会变成致命的拖累，因为根本没有一个强权机构能强制所有节点立刻同步更新。在这场跟死神的赛跑中，杂乱无章的逃生指令只会让 $NEWT 的价格体系遭遇毫无缓冲的硬着陆。#newt 
面对这种悬顶之剑，用户必须把眼光放长远。首先，趁早扔掉那份天真，你要明白“先收集后破解”是黑客的惯用伎俩，那些已经被传统算法封装并沉淀下来的敏感资产，未来注定是要被扒光的。其次，去按住项目方的头，要他们立马交出详尽的测试网演练计划和过渡期风控细则，拿不出干货就是在画大饼。最后，如果你的文件价值连城，唯一的土办法就是自己动手：在 Newton 的通道之外，先用独立的后量子工具把文件锁死，然后再传。代码架构再优雅也扛不住算力降维，只有你自己加上去的物理防线，才是最后那根救命稻草。#eth $ETH

title: 逃不掉的“中间态”泥潭：深度拆解 $NEWT 白皮书不敢提的量子危机
subTitle:
深夜死磕 Newton Protocol 的白皮书第11节，看到那套关于“密码学长寿命”的说辞，但凡有点工程常识的人都会觉得后背发凉。官方字里行间用了一个极其傲慢的定语：“当后量子密码学成熟时”。注意，他们没用“万一”，而是“当”。这说明什么？说明项目方在拿一个尚未落地的技术大饼，来平息你眼前的恐慌。他们拍胸脯保证，未来只要“动动配置”，就能把底层的 X25519 换成 ML-KEM。这根本不是严谨的路线图，而是在贩卖信仰——让你掏钱买定离手，赌量子霸权不会在他们大功告成前提前降临。@NewtonProtocol 

Newton 确实用了 HPKE 架构，白皮书也死命吹嘘这种架构的“算法敏捷性”。说白了，这就叫底层热插拔。但项目方最鸡贼的地方在于，他们把这种“未来方便换锁”的机制，包装成了“你现在的数据绝对安全”。别被高大上的词汇忽悠了，你当下在链上交互的所有隐私，依旧是靠传统的椭圆曲线算法在防守。这层防御在真正的量子算力面前，薄得连张草纸都不如。他们的潜台词其实是：等黑客快杀到了我们再搬家，现在你先凑合着住。

咱们把底层基元的遮羞布扯下来。现在的 ECDSA 和 BLS 签名，命门全在离散对数问题上。面对搭载 Shor 算法的量子机器，被秒杀只是多项式时间内的必然，这是数学铁律，没得商量。虽然 NIST 今年急匆匆推出了 ML-KEM 和 ML-DSA 这种抗量子标准，但那都是刚出炉的半成品。学术界还在天天拿着放大镜找漏洞，去年那个被寄予厚望的 Rainbow 方案，不到一个周末就被一台家用电脑直接锤爆。这种连安全边界都没彻底摸透的玩意儿，哪来的底气说能无缝衔接？$NEWT 

最可笑的是，官方把这种底层大挪移轻描淡写地称为“配置变更”。懂行的人都知道，新老两套算法的数学逻辑根本不挨着，私钥格式完全不通用。真到了要切的那天，全网所有用户的旧钥匙必须全部作废，历史存证全得用新格式再裹一遍，节点运营商更是得硬着头皮重跑分布式网络。一旦用户量上了规模，这叫改配置？这明明是把整个生态拉上手术台，不打麻药直接做开膛破肚的换心手术。#newt 

还有个官方死活不敢细聊的黑洞，那就是新旧交替的“过渡期”。在漫长的升级过程中，网络里绝对是旧钥匙和新钥匙混着跑。密码学圈子早有共识，这种“双轨制”是最容易翻车的高危区。当年 OpenSSH 就吃过这种血亏，黑客利用混合模式的漏洞，直接实施降级攻击，强迫系统用回最弱的老算法。Newton 搞的这种模块化拼接，在混乱的过渡期，简直就是给攻击者疯狂递刀子。

这套把戏，直接绑架了 $NEWT 的市场底线。试想一下，一旦哪天谷歌或 IBM 突然宣布量子计算攻克了某个关键节点，哪怕只是跑通了个阉割版的算法，整个加密圈和古典金融界也会瞬间炸锅。到那时候，谁还有耐心听你解释什么“平滑过渡”？恐慌一旦蔓延，Newton 那引以为傲的去中心化就会变成最致命的累赘——节点根本没法强制统一行动。在与量子时钟的生死竞速中，这种混乱的踩踏会把 $NEWT 的代币价格毫无悬念地砸穿。

所以，别拿自己的身家性命去赌项目方的公关话术。第一，别心存侥幸，那些现在就被黑客截获囤积起来的数据，一旦量子突破，立刻全裸，未来的升级救不了你昨天发出的数据。第二，死盯开发进度，逼他们交出具体的测试网时间表和混合期安全方案，拿不出来就是耍流氓。最后，要是你的数据真金贵到了极点，最管用的土办法就是：在 Newton 的协议外面，你自己人工再套一层抗量子加密。虽然操作起来笨重且难看，但在降维打击面前，多一层的物理冗余，才是真命根子。#eth $ETH

translatedData.title: The “in-between state” quagmire you can’t escape: a deep dissection of the quantum crisis the NEWT whitepaper won’t mention
translatedData.subTitle: At midnight, I pored over Section 11 of the Newton Protocol whitepaper, and saw that line of reasoning about “cryptographic longevity.” Anyone with a bit of engineering sense would feel their spine go cold. In the official text, between the lines, there’s an extremely arrogant modifier: “when post-quantum cryptography becomes mature.” Notice they didn’t say “if”—they said “when.” What does that mean? It means the project team is using an as-yet-unrealized technical fantasy to soothe the panic you’re feeling right now. They loudly promise that all it takes is to “just tweak the configuration” in the future to swap the underlying X25519 with ML-KEM. This isn’t a rigorous roadmap at all—it’s faith-selling: get you to pay upfront, place your bet, and hope that quantum supremacy won’t arrive early and disrupt their grand success before they finish.\u003cm-20/\u003e

title: 零赔付与高垄断：透视 $NEWT 票仓背后的利益内循环
subTitle:
Newton Protocol 白皮书里白纸黑字写的“许可制节点”，其实是个极度危险的信号。一旦放弃了谁都能进的无门槛机制，转而搞什么背景审查，这套系统的信任底座就从机器变成了人。官方拿“方便问责”来打掩护，但问题是，如果看大门的人自己心术不正，这道门禁到底防了谁？

更要命的是规则谁来定。在他们的设计里，$NEWT 筹码多的人说了算。这就形成了一个无解的死循环：链上数据是蒙着脸的，你根本摸不清那些在提案里投赞成票的持币大鳄，是不是早就跟现在的节点老板串通好了。当裁判和运动员是一拨人时，他们完全能不动声色地把准入条件变成一堵挡风墙，把同行死死挡在外面。

咱们推演个最狠的清场套路。假设现在盘子里有25家在跑节点，其中十几家是大户的马甲。他们只要在社区里喊一句“我们要更安全”，顺势砸出一个强制要求百万级美金安全审计的提案。头部玩家利润丰厚，这点血出得起；可那些草根技术大神哪掏得出这笔巨款？最后只能灰溜溜走人。人走茶凉，剩下的几个老油条就把利润全吞了。

官方最爱干的事，就是拿 $NEWT 的庞大质押数字出来稳定军心。似乎只要池子里的钱够多，这套体系就固若金汤。但这纯粹是偷换概念。高质押额顶多能让外部黑客望而却步，却防不住内部人作妖。当网络里的有效节点越来越少，这帮人想搞点小动作，甚至连个像样的阻力都遇不到，这种脆弱根本不是用钱能填平的。@NewtonProtocol 

明面上的集中还能看见，最怕的是底层的同质化暗礁。看着节点分布图五彩斑斓，其实大家私底下可能都在用同一家云主机的同一套解决方案，甚至连服务器代码的漏洞都是一模一样的。万一这些节点刚好都归同一个强势的监管机构管辖呢？这种牵一发而动全身的隐患，在他们那套精美的估值模型里，半个字都没提。

这种雷一旦引爆，就是连环车祸。设想某个工作日，某家头部云服务商机房宕机。因为底层架构高度重合，Newton 网络里一大半的机器瞬间失联。签名不够，网络直接停摆。这根本不是什么偶发的技术故障，而是为了堆砌所谓“高质量节点”指标，彻底抛弃去中心化多样性所招致的必然惩罚。#newt 

真到了网络瘫痪那一刻，利益受损的层级极其荒谬。没错，链停了，NEWT代币价格肯定会跟着跳水。但对于那些早就赚得盆满钵满的持币庄家来说，这顶多叫利润回撤。可对于那些把身家性命押在上面的生态项目方呢？用户无法提现，核心业务停滞，这种实打实的真金白银蒸发，全砸在了毫无准备的散户和开发者头上。

整个游戏最黑的地方就在这里：信息被彻底掐断了。生态里的应用方老老实实交着网费，却根本无权知晓底层节点到底绑得有多紧。没有风险披露，没有赔付准备金，所有人都在为一个不知何时引爆的定时炸弹买单。等到潮水退去，Newton Protocol 里的赢家早就套现离场，只留下一地鸡毛让真正的使用者去扫。#eth $ETH

title: 质押量不等于安全：一文看透 Newton Protocol 底层架构的连环死穴
subTitle:
翻开 Newton Protocol 的设定集，第9.2节里那个“许可制”标签，简直就是一枚埋得极深的软钉子。这根本不是什么为了抗审查而做的技术妥协，而是赤裸裸的权力寻租。把去中心化网络生生降级成一个需要靠人工画圈子才能进的俱乐部，表面上说是为了好追责，但只要这套筛选尺子捏在有心人手里，整条防线分分钟形同虚设。
谁来负责发这张入场券？答案是代币投票。这就搞出了一个堪称完美的利益内循环。你根本没法顺着链上的匿名马甲，查出那些举手赞成的 $NEWT 持币大户，跟后台跑机器的节点老板是不是同一个人。一旦他们穿的是同一条裤子，所谓的“社区共识”，无非就是小圈子用来砌高围墙、独占收益的合法外衣罢了。
咱们设想一个最残忍的洗盘局：盘子里现在有25个席位，其中15个被几头巨鲸暗中控盘。他们随便找个“提升网络安全”的由头，强行通过一项新规，要求所有节点每年必须自费扛下一笔天价的第三方美元审计。对那些早就吃饱喝足的既得利益者来说，这点钱就是洒洒水；但对于纯靠技术吃饭、口袋空空的独立开发团队，这无疑是张驱逐令。人被赶走了，空出来的肉自然就落到了寡头碗里。#newt @NewtonProtocol 
Newton 官方特别喜欢拿“质押总量”来给自己贴金，仿佛池子里的钱越多，安全底座就越牢不可破。但他们绝口不提另一个致命指标——内部串谋难度。即便NEWT的锁仓金额一分没少，只要干活的节点数量越来越少、越来越抱团，系统内部作恶的门槛就会直线跳水。这就像是在炫耀金库的防盗门有多厚，却对里头的保安早已经拜了同一个大哥这件事闭口不谈。
比台面上的抱团更让人后背发凉的，是底层的“连带死穴”。节点在地图上看着星罗棋布，欧亚美洲哪哪都有，但这很可能只是个迷魂阵。要是他们背地里全在薅同一家云厂商的同一个机房，或者系统里都跑着同一个没打补丁的软件框架，甚至连肉身都处在同一个监管铁拳的阴影下呢？这种暗藏的结构性黑天鹅，白皮书里根本没有给它标价。
这种雷一旦炸开，就是毁灭性的。假设某个平常的下午，主流云服务商突然拉闸。就因为这层隐秘的底层捆绑，Newton 网上过半数的节点瞬间暴毙。签名凑不齐，出块直接卡死。这不是什么概率极小的代码bug，而是为了追求所谓的“高质量节点”，放弃生态多样性后必然遭到的系统性反噬。
到了真出事那一刻，你会发现代价的分配极其畸形。网络罢工，收不到过路费，$NEWT 的代币价格确实会跟着大跳水。但持币大佬们的亏损是有底线的，大不了就是账面浮亏。而那些真金白银把业务搭在这个协议上的应用方呢？交易发不出去、资产被恶意清算、业务全面停摆，这些像大山一样砸下来的真实现金流损失，只能由他们自己咬碎牙往肚子里咽。
这就是这套玩法最鸡贼的地方。应用生态在毫不知情的情况下，为一种压根没被公开的单点故障风险支付着全额的Gas费。市场没有要求风险溢价，因为信息被死死捂住了。大家都在为一张所谓的“优质网络”买单，直到某天隐患彻底引爆。到时候，面对那张长长的停机账单，割韭菜的在VIP室里装死，而掏钱补窟窿的，永远是底下的终端用户。#eth $ETH

translatedData.title: Staked Amount Doesn’t Equal Security: One Article Exposes the Newton Protocol’s Underlying Architectural Chain of Failures
translatedData.subTitle:
Open the Newton Protocol configuration manual and go to Section 9.2—the “permit system” tag there is basically a soft tack buried extremely deep. This isn’t a technical compromise made to resist censorship; it’s a blatant case of power rental. By degrading a decentralized network into a club that requires people to manually draw circles to get in, they claim it’s for accountability—but as long as those filtering gauges are held by the right-minded individuals, the entire line of defense becomes meaningless in minutes.
Who is responsible for issuing this admission ticket? The answer is token voting. That creates an almost perfect self-reinforcing interest loop. You can’t trace, from the chain’s anonymous aliases, the large token holders who voted in favor—nor can you determine whether the node operators running backend machines are the same person. Once they’re wearing the same pair of pants, so-called “community consensus” is nothing more than a legal cloak for a small circle to build high walls and exclusively capture the gains.

title: Ethereum: More Than a Cryptocurrency—It's the Engine Behind Web3
subTitle:
When people first discover crypto, Bitcoin is usually the first name they hear. But the deeper they explore the blockchain world, the more they realize that Ethereum is where much of the real innovation happens.

Unlike Bitcoin, which was created primarily as a decentralized form of digital money, Ethereum was designed with a much broader vision. It introduced the idea that blockchain technology could power applications, agreements, financial services, and even entire digital communities without relying on banks or centralized companies. That vision has transformed Ethereum into one of the most influential blockchain networks in the world.

At the heart of Ethereum are smart contracts—self-executing programs that automatically carry out transactions when specific conditions are met. Instead of depending on intermediaries, these contracts allow people to exchange value, build businesses, and create applications in a transparent and secure way. This innovation has made Ethereum the foundation of decentralized finance, NFTs, blockchain gaming, and countless Web3 projects.

ETH, Ethereum's native cryptocurrency, plays a central role in this ecosystem. Every time someone interacts with an application on the Ethereum network, they use ETH to pay transaction fees. It's not just a digital asset people buy and sell—it's the fuel that keeps the network running.

One of Ethereum's most significant milestones came with its transition from Proof of Work to Proof of Stake. This upgrade dramatically reduced the network's energy consumption while improving its long-term sustainability. Instead of miners competing with expensive hardware, validators now help secure the blockchain by staking their ETH, making the network far more energy-efficient than before.

What makes Ethereum stand out isn't only its technology but also the strength of its community. Thousands of developers continue building innovative applications on the network, while businesses and institutions increasingly recognize its potential. As blockchain adoption grows, Ethereum remains at the center of many of the industry's biggest developments.

Of course, Ethereum is still a cryptocurrency, which means its price can be highly volatile. Market sentiment, global economic conditions, regulations, technological upgrades, and investor confidence all influence its value. Like any investment, it carries both opportunities and risks.

Ethereum isn't trying to compete with Bitcoin by becoming digital gold. Instead, it has carved out its own role as the infrastructure powering a decentralized internet. Whether it's enabling financial services without banks, supporting digital ownership, or giving developers the tools to build the next generation of applications, Ethereum continues to shape the future of blockchain technology.

For anyone interested in crypto, understanding Ethereum is about more than following its price. It's about recognizing how one blockchain has evolved into the foundation of an entirely new digital economy—and why millions of people believe its journey is only getting started.

#Ethereum  #ETH  #Crypto  #Blockchain  #Web3

title: Ethereum — больше, чем просто деньги
subTitle:
Ethereum: Интернет, которым владеешь ты
Представь интернет, где приложениями не управляют гиганты вроде Google или Apple. В этом интернете нет банков, которые решают, можно ли тебе перевести деньги, и нет посредников, которые берут комиссию за каждый твой шаг. Вот это и есть Ethereum.
Как это работает на простом примере?
Обычные приложения — это «закрытые коробки». Ты просто пользуешься ими, а все данные и правила устанавливает владелец. Ethereum — это «открытый фундамент». На нем можно построить что угодно: от кошелька для денег до игры или соцсети. Но главное — никто не может заблокировать твою страницу или заморозить твои активы, потому что сеть принадлежит всем сразу и никому конкретно.
Почему об этом все говорят?
Полный контроль. Только у тебя есть ключи от твоих цифровых денег и вещей. Никакой «админ» не может забрать их у тебя.
Честность. Вместо того чтобы доверять банку или компании на слово, мы доверяем программному коду. Его нельзя обмануть или «подкрутить» под себя.
Универсальность. Сегодня Ethereum используют для всего: от быстрых переводов денег в любую точку мира до создания уникальных цифровых предметов коллекционирования.
Суть проста: если биткоин — это способ просто хранить деньги, то Ethereum — это целая платформа, на которой работает новый интернет. Интернет, где ты — не просто пользователь, а полноправный владелец того, что делаешь.

1、背景

以太坊基金会最新披露，Protocol Security团队已将一组AI代理正式用于“红队测试”，目标直指ETH生态底层依赖软件，包括密码学组件、协议实现与智能合约安全。此次最受关注的进展，是AI代理在以太坊共识客户端依赖的libp2p gossipsub层中，发现了可被远程触发的panic类漏洞，且相关问题已完成修复并公开登记。这个信号很重要：AI不再只是辅助写代码或做审计摘要，而是开始进入真实攻防场景，参与漏洞挖掘、路径推演和结果验证。🤖

2、核心分析

从披露内容看，这套AI安全体系并非单一模型“通吃”，而是采用分工式代理架构，包括侦察、搜索、补缺、验证等角色。这样的设计更接近真实安全团队协作模式：先识别潜在攻击面，再尝试复现，再确认是否影响生产环境。相比传统人工审计，AI代理的优势在于覆盖面广、试错速度快、可持续运行，尤其适合以太坊这种代码库庞大、客户端多样、组件耦合复杂的系统。

但更值得注意的是，基金会同时强调，AI并未替代安全研究员。原因很现实：AI可以快速生成“看似合理”的漏洞链路，却未必都成立。在高价值公链场景中，误报和伪结论的成本很高，因此最终仍需要资深研究员进行筛查、复现和定性。这意味着，AI在安全领域的真正价值，不是完全自动化，而是把专家资源从重复性工作中释放出来，让人工精力集中到高风险问题的判断和处置上。

3、行业影响

这一进展对ETH和更广泛的Crypto行业都有启发。首先，它说明头部公链正在把安全投入前移，从“漏洞出现后修复”转向“持续对抗式发现”。其次，AI代理如果能在底层网络层发现真实漏洞，未来也可能被扩展到桥、Rollup、MEV相关组件及DeFi协议中，推动安全测试进入更高频、更自动化阶段。对市场而言，这类消息短期未必直接推升价格，但会增强外界对以太坊基础设施韧性的信心。📌

4、结论

综合来看，这不是一则单纯的“发现漏洞”新闻，而是一次安全方法论升级。以太坊基金会释放出的关键信号是：未来协议安全竞争，不只比代码质量，也比谁能更早建立“AI+人工”的混合防御体系。对开发者、审计机构和基础设施项目方而言，如何利用AI提升漏洞发现效率，同时控制误报风险，将成为当前阶段的重要课题。

#ETH #Ethereum #crypto

title: ETH at $1,746 Is Stuck Between a Yawn and a Breakout
subTitle:
Ethereum is doing that thing again — the thing where it sits in the middle of a range and dares you to care. Per CoinMarketCap, ETH is trading at $1,745.91 on Binance, up a mighty 0.12% over the last 24 hours. Somewhere, a leveraged trader just closed a position and wondered why they bothered.

But here is the thing about boring price action: it is usually the setup, not the punchline.

Let me paint the board for you. ETH has carved out a 72-hour support at $1,713.44 and resistance at $1,833.40 on Binance. That gives us a roughly $120 corridor — and right now, the price is sitting near the lower third of that band. Not exactly screaming "moon," but not falling apart either. The 24-hour volume clocked in at $303.19 million, and the market cap holds at $210.09 billion according to CoinMarketCap. Those are not crisis numbers. Those are "waiting for a catalyst" numbers.

So what are the catalysts floating around? The headlines today are a cocktail of AI hype, political overreach, and options expiry drama — none of it directly about ETH, which is part of the problem. Bitcoin miners are pivoting to AI and getting side-eyed by investors over insider sales. UK politicians are mulling a permanent crypto donation ban, because apparently the best way to handle a scandal is to ban the entire asset class. And the big one: Bitcoin has a $1.4 billion options expiry on Friday, with everyone asking if BTC can hold $62K. That kind of event tends to drag the whole market into its gravity — ETH included.

Here is the honest read beneath the noise. ETH does not have its own headline catalyst right now. There is no ETF flow frenzy dominating the tape, no major network upgrade imminent, no Vitalik tweetstorm moving markets. The on-chain activity is steady but unspectacular. What ETH has is a well-defined technical range and a market that is collectively waiting to see which side gives first.

And that is actually useful information.

If ETH holds the $1,713.44 support, the range stays intact. That level is the floor where buyers have stepped in over the past 72 hours, and as long as it holds, the dip-buy logic remains valid. Every touch of support that bounces is a small signal that someone with size is defending it. If you are watching for an entry, the area around that support is the zone where risk is most clearly defined — you know exactly where the thesis breaks.

If ETH loses $1,713.44, though, the range breaks down. That opens the door to a momentum flush, and given the lack of an ETH-specific narrative to catch a falling knife, the next support is not guaranteed to show up quickly. Sellers would have the upper hand.

On the flip side, if ETH pushes up toward and through the $1,833.40 resistance, that changes the character of the chart entirely. A clean break above that level would flip the range ceiling into a floor, and that is where momentum traders start paying attention. Until then, resistance is the wall where sellers have capped every rally attempt in this window.

Meanwhile, SENT is up 21.3% today according to CoinMarketCap, which is the kind of random altcoin pump that reminds you the market still has a pulse — even if ETH is not the one doing the jumping. The risk-on appetite is there in pockets. It just has not landed on the second-largest crypto yet.

So the question becomes: is this a coiled spring waiting for the Bitcoin expiry dust to settle, or is it a slow drift lower while attention goes elsewhere?

The levels are clear. The range is defined. The catalyst is missing — which, in crypto, often means it is about to show up.

The $ETH pair is one tap away when you want to act on these exact levels. Support and resistance are both in view, and the next few days — shaped by that Friday options expiry and whatever macro headline drops next — will decide which one matters more.

Laugh, then look at the chart.

The Upside Scenario: 
The Path to + $4,500
My primary thesis is moderately bullish, and I expect Ethereum to break out of its current consolidation phase and target the $4,200 – $4,500 range before the end of the year. Here is why:

The Staking Deflationary Spiral: Unlike previous cycles, a massive percentage of circulating $ETH  is now locked in staking contracts. This creates a structural supply shock. As decentralized applications (dApps) and Layer-2 networks demand more gas, the token-burning mechanism (
EIP−1559
) will accelerate, making ETH highly deflationary during high-activity months.

Institutional Liquidity Maturation: The initial hype of institutional products has settled into a phase of steady, quiet accumulation. Wealth managers are slowly adding #ETH  to diversified portfolios as a "tech-index" asset, establishing a strong price floor that didn't exist in previous years.

Layer-2 Dominance: While critics argue that Layer-2 networks steal mainnet volume, they actually solidify Ethereum as the ultimate settlement layer. The cheaper the L2 transactions get, the more users enter the ecosystem, ultimately driving value back to Layer-1.

⚠️ The Downside Scenario: The Risk of Distribution
No asset moves in a straight line. If the market faces a bearish turn, I expect $ETH to heavily test macro support around $2,800 – $3,000. The triggers for this would be:

Regulatory Fatigue: Any unexpected regulatory pressure on decentralized finance (DeFi) protocols or staking providers could trigger a short-term panic and mass unstaking.

Capital Rotation to Alternatives: If high-throughput layer-1 competitors capture a disproportionate share of retail meme-coin speculative volume, Ethereum might experience a temporary stagnation in momentum, delaying its breakout.

Tether Mints 1 Billion USDT Again: The Stablecoin Printing Press Is Back—What Is the Market Betting On?

Tether has once again minted 1 billion USDT on the TRON network. This isn’t the first time, and it won’t be the last. Justin Sun immediately announced that the TRC20-USDT supply has surpassed $90 billion, calling it a “critical moment” for Tether and TRON.

In plain terms: the stablecoin giant is accelerating expansion, and TRON has become the largest channel for USDT circulation.

1. Minting ≠ immediate inflow to the market. Tether’s usual pattern is “mint first, then backfill”—it creates inventory on-chain in advance, then releases it gradually based on market demand. But frequent large mints themselves send a signal: institutional demand for USDT is picking up.

2. What does $90 billion TRC20-USDT mean? TRON carries the absolute majority of USDT circulation globally. It offers fast transfers and low fees, making it especially friendly to Asian markets. Tether’s decision to keep adding to TRON indicates its core user base is still expanding.

3. The real impact on the market: USDT issuance typically comes with two scenarios—either (1) ammunition reserves before institutions move in with large orders, or (2) a rise in demand for hedging during periods of market volatility. With BTC holding above 63,000 and the funding rate staying near 0.007%, market sentiment is fairly neutral. This minting is more likely to be the former.

4. Signals to watch out for: if, after the USDT increase, there isn’t a clear risk-asset inflow—and instead the funds settle in exchanges or on-chain wallets—then institutions are still on the sidelines. The real market move requires seeing stablecoins shift from “reserves” to “deployed capital.”

One-sentence summary: Tether is printing money, but it hasn’t been spent yet. The market is waiting for an ignition signal.

Tether再铸10亿USDT：稳定币印钞机重启，市场在赌什么？

Tether 在波场 TRON 网络再次铸造 10 亿枚 USDT。这不是第一次，也不会是最后一次。孙宇晨随即宣布 TRC20-USDT 发行量突破 900 亿美元，称这是 Tether 和波场的「关键时刻」。

翻译一下：稳定币巨头正在加速扩张，而 TRON 成了 USDT 最大的流通管道。

1. 铸造 ≠ 立即流入市场。Tether 的惯例是「先铸后备」——提前在链上创建库存，再根据市场需求逐步释放。但频繁的大额铸造本身就释放了信号：机构端对 USDT 的需求在回升。

2. 900 亿 TRC20-USDT 意味着什么？波场网络承载了全球 USDT 流通量的绝对大头，转账速度快、手续费低，对亚洲市场尤其友好。Tether 选择持续加码 TRON，说明其用户基本盘仍在扩张。

3. 对市场的实际影响：USDT 增发通常伴随两种场景——一是机构大额入场前的弹药储备，二是市场波动期避险需求的上升。当前 BTC 站稳 63000 上方，资金费率维持在 0.007% 附近，市场情绪偏中性，此次铸造更可能是前者。

4. 需要警惕的信号：如果 USDT 增发后并未伴随明显的资金流入风险资产，而是沉淀在交易所或链上钱包，说明机构仍在观望。真正的行情启动，需要看到稳定币从「储备」变成「 deployed capital」。

一句话总结：Tether 在印钞，但钱还没花出去。市场在等一个点火信号。

title: Capital Is Quietly Dripping Into One Corner of the Market
subTitle:
Picture a room full of traders at the end of a long shift. Nobody is running toward the exits, but nobody is charging through a new door either. That is what the tape feels like right now across the majors — a market catching its breath, scanning for the next catalyst, and quietly deciding where the next dollar goes.

Start with the big picture. Bitcoin is making headlines again after pushing past $63,000 on the back of geopolitical noise out of Washington. Traders are glued to the $62,000 level ahead of a $1.4 billion options expiry on Friday, and that gravitational pull is affecting everything underneath it. When Bitcoin churns in a range, capital does not just sit idle — it rotates, and the order flow tells you exactly where it is landing.

Right now the rotation story runs through two lanes: the heavyweight that is coiling near support, and the faster layer-1 that refuses to break down.

Ethereum is the more interesting setup of the two. According to CoinMarketCap, $ETH sits at $1,735.29 on Binance with a market cap north of $209 billion and 24-hour spot volume of $309.90 million. That volume dwarfs most altcoin order books combined, which means when ETH moves, it moves with real liquidity behind it. The problem — or the opportunity, depending on your lens — is that price is hovering just $22 above the 72-hour support at $1,713.44. Resistance up at $1,833.40 is still nearly a hundred dollars away. That is a wide corridor, and the tape is telling you that buyers have shown up twice already to defend that lower band. If $1,713.44 holds through the next few sessions, the dip-buy zone is defined and the path of least resistance tilts back toward mid-range. If it loses that floor on a clean candle close, the order book thins out quickly and the next resting bid is not obvious from this data alone. That is the kind of binary setup that gets institutional desks to lean in.

Meanwhile $SOL is doing something subtly different. At $77.50 per CoinMarketCap, it sits just above its own 72-hour support of $76.29, with resistance capping action at $83.74. The 24-hour gain is a modest 0.27 percent, but what matters is the structure: SOL has tested that $76 level repeatedly and bounced without panic selling. Market cap at $45.10 billion and daily volume of $119.64 million confirm that this is not a thin-market illusion. If buyers hold $76.29 through this consolidation, the measured move targets the $83 resistance band. If it cracks, the same logic applies — the next support is not printed on your 72-hour chart, which means you are flying without a floor.

Zoom out and the narrative writes itself. Capital is not fleeing the market. It is parking in the two names with the deepest books and the cleanest technical maps, waiting for a reason to commit. The macro catalysts are lining up — the Friday options expiry, the MARA infrastructure deal signaling institutional crypto-adjacent demand, and the political headlines out of the UK adding regulatory uncertainty that tends to push volume back into the most liquid pairs.

Here is the human takeaway: the market is not giving you a screaming entry on anything right now. It is giving you a well-defined range with clear floors and ceilings, which is actually more valuable because it lets you plan instead of chase. Ethereum in particular is sitting in a spot where one more test of that $1,713 support either confirms the floor or opens a new leg down — and the next 24 to 48 hours will likely decide which.

If you want to position around that level while the setup is still live, the $ETH pair is one tap away. The levels are on your screen, the volume is real, and the range is defined.

Read the tape, not the noise.

Not financial advice.

#newt $NEWT If policy execution becomes a new infrastructure, NEWT’s biggest fear isn’t that nobody will use it—it’s that everyone will use it differently.
I worked on API standardization in Copenhagen, and what I feared most was a platform suddenly becoming “too flexible.” If every customer can customize everything and every team can tweak parameters, it may seem friendly in the short term, but in the long run it turns into a maintenance nightmare.
If Newton’s policy execution becomes infrastructure, it will face the same problem. Different vaults, RWAs, stablecoins, and AI agents all want their own rules. Some prioritize address screening, others prioritize price tolerances, others prioritize identity restrictions, and others prioritize quota controls. The more people use it, the more fragmented the rules become.
Not being used is obviously a risk. But when everyone uses it in different ways, that’s also a risk. Audit tools become hard to compare, users can’t easily understand it, developers can’t adapt, and operators have to deal with ever more complex combinations of rules. In the end, Newton may not be a single unified authorization layer—it may turn into a set of separate, incompatible rule islands.#ETH 
The solution isn’t to restrict customization—it’s to establish baseline standards. At minimum, every policy should have consistent tags, a risk level, version history, and a standardized description format. That way, different projects can tailor their needs, but users can still compare them.#BTC 
For NEWT to truly take on policy execution, it can’t only chase the number of integrations. It also needs to make the ecosystem understand: even though these rules differ, they can all be interpreted, audited, and held accountable in the same language. Otherwise, the more it’s used, the more chaotic the system becomes.@NewtonProtocol

content:
#newt $NEWT 如果政策执行成了新基础设施，NEWT 最怕的不是没人用，而是大家用法各不相同
我在哥本哈根做过 API 标准化，最怕一个平台突然“太灵活”。每个客户都能自定义，每个团队都能改参数，短期看很友好，长期看就是维护地狱。
Newton 的 policy 执行如果变成基础设施，也会遇到这个问题。不同 vault、RWA、稳定币、AI agent 都想要自己的规则。有人重视地址筛查，有人重视价格容差，有人重视身份限制，有人重视额度控制。用的人越多，规则越分散。
没人用当然是风险，但大家用法各不相同，也是一种风险。审计工具难以比较，用户难以理解，开发者难以适配，operator 也要面对越来越复杂的规则组合。最后 Newton 可能不是一个统一授权层，而是一堆互不相通的规则小岛。#ETH 
解决办法不是限制自定义，而是建立基础标准。至少要让每条 policy 有统一标签、风险等级、版本记录和说明格式。这样不同项目可以定制，但用户仍然能比较。#BTC 
NEWT 真正要承接政策执行，就不能只追求接入数量。它还要让生态知道：这些规则虽然不同，但都能被同一种语言解释、审计和追责。否则用得越多，系统越乱。@NewtonProtocol

title: 当授权层开始替交易排序，NEWT 需要解释谁排在前面、谁被放到后面
subTitle:
我在纽约做过订单路由分析，最敏感的永远不是价格，而是顺序。谁先被看到，谁先被处理，谁先拿到流动性，谁就可能拿走利润。很多系统表面上说自己只是通道，最后都绕不开排序权。#Newt $NEWT 
Newton 如果只是交易前检查，那问题还相对简单：符合规则就放，不符合就拦。但一旦它成为更多 DeFi vault、RWA、稳定币和 AI agent 的授权入口，它就不只是检查器，也可能变成入口队列。交易不是孤立到达的。高峰期、活动期、市场波动期，大量 intent 同时进来，系统就必须决定先处理谁。
这时候，排序权会浮出水面。
谁排在前面？费用高的？风险低的？机构客户？高质押 operator 推荐的任务？历史信誉好的应用？还是纯粹按时间先后？如果这些规则不透明，授权层就会从安全基础设施悄悄变成优先级市场。
不要小看这件事。对普通转账来说，慢几秒可能没什么；对清算、套利、vault 调仓、稳定币赎回来说，顺序就是价格。一个 intent 晚处理十几秒，可能错过窗口；一个高价值任务被优先处理，可能挤掉小用户请求。授权层如果掌握入口队列，就必须解释排队规则。
NEWT 在这里可能会变得很微妙。如果费用、质押、服务等级和 operator 选择都与 NEWT 相关，那市场自然会问：持有更多 NEWT 或支付更高费用，是否能获得更快评估？如果能，这是合理的服务分层，还是链上金融的新 VIP 通道？如果不能，网络在拥堵时如何分配有限资源？
我不反对优先级。现实金融里，机构专线、做市商通道、高等级 API 都存在。问题是，Web3 不能一边讲公平开放，一边把排序权藏在后台。只要优先级存在，就应该公开：任务队列怎么排序，哪些因素影响处理速度，拥堵时是否有降级机制，小额用户是否会长期排在后面。
Newton 未来最该公开的不只是通过率和拒绝率，还包括队列数据。平均等待时间、不同任务类型等待时间、费用层级差异、operator 路由分布、失败重试次数、拥堵时被延迟的任务占比。这些指标听起来不性感，但它们决定用户是不是真的被公平对待。#ETH 
AI agent 场景尤其需要这个透明度。一个自动化策略提交 intent 后，如果被排到后面，它可能仍然“正确执行”，但市场条件已经变了。用户最后亏钱时，表面看是策略问题，实则可能是授权层排队慢半拍。没有队列记录，责任很难说清。
我更希望 Newton 把授权层做成可审计的交通系统，而不是看不见的收费通道。红绿灯怎么亮重要，车道怎么排也重要。快车道可以有，但必须标出来；慢车道也可以存在，但不能让用户误以为自己在同一条路上。#BTC 
NEWT 如果要支撑这套网络，就不能只讲“交易前安全”。它还要面对入口资源分配。安全检查本身会占用计算、数据、operator 和证明资源。资源一旦有限，排序就不可避免。排序一旦不可避免，透明就是底线。
授权层开始替交易排序的那天，Newton 就不再只是门卫，而像调度员。门卫只决定能不能进，调度员决定谁先进。金融世界里，调度权从来不是小事。
@NewtonProtocol

translatedData.title: When the authorization layer starts to influence transaction ordering, NEWT needs to explain who goes first and who gets pushed back
translatedData.subTitle:
I did order routing analysis in New York. The most sensitive thing is never the price, but the order. Whoever is seen first, processed first, and receives liquidity first may end up taking the profits. Many systems claim on the surface that they are just a conduit, but in the end they can’t escape ordering power. #Newt $NEWT 
If Newton is only used for pre-trade checks, the problem is relatively simple: if it matches the rules, let it through; if not, block it. But once it becomes the authorized entry point for more DeFi vaults, RWA, stablecoins, and AI agents, it’s no longer just a checker—it can also become an entry queue. Transactions don’t arrive in isolation. During peak times, event periods, and market volatility, lots of intents come in at the same time, and the system has to decide who to process first.

Bitcoin (BTC) may be breaking away from its dependence on Michael Saylor’s Strategy (Nasdaq: MSTR), and institutional investors are becoming the next major source of demand.

BTC “ignores” Strategy’s recent selloff
In an interview with Milk Road on July 8, Matt Hougan, Chief Investment Officer at Bitwise, said that while Strategy has been the primary buyer of Bitcoin over the past few years, that role is weakening.
Hougan added, “It will still be important, but it is no longer the main source of marginal capital.” He noted that after Strategy sold slightly more than $200 million worth of Bitcoin to pay preferred stock dividends, Bitcoin’s price reacted with little enthusiasm.
He said Bitcoin “doesn’t care about this,” and believes the market will view the selloff as evidence of Strategy taking rational action rather than a signal of forced liquidation under pressure.
After the selloff, Bitcoin rebounded back to the $64,000 level—its first return to that mark in nearly two weeks.

Bitwise research head Ryan Rasmussen said clients are still asking whether Strategy poses concentration risk, but most people believe it is no longer a major long-term risk for Bitcoin.

The next buyer is the “ultimate boss” in investing
Hougan said Bitcoin’s history has been defined by one major buyer passing the baton to the next: from crypto punks to Asian retail investors, U.S. retail investors, GBTC, Strategy—now it’s institutional capital’s turn.
Hougan said, “The next marginal buyer is the ultimate boss in investing—that is institutional capital.”
Rasmussen said Vanguard is looking for a digital asset executive, which is another sign of traditional finance pushing further into the crypto space.
He said institutional adoption is forming a “wave.” As customers and peers enter this asset class, asset managers, advisors, pension funds, and endowment funds increasingly have to consider allocating to crypto assets.
Hougan added that Wall Street’s professional risk has reversed.
Earlier, supporting cryptocurrencies could hurt professionals’ reputations. He said now, ignoring digital assets may actually carry greater risk.
Bitwise also emphasized that decentralized finance (DeFi) assets have recently performed strongly. Although the overall crypto market has been weak, the company’s DeFi index rose 51% over the past three months.

Hougan補充道：「它仍將很重要，但不再是邊際資金的主要來源。」他指出，在Strategy出售了略高於$2億的比特幣以支付優先股股息後，比特幣價格反應平淡。
他表示，比特幣「對此毫不在意」，並認爲市場將此次拋售視爲Strategy理性操作的證據，而非迫於壓力進行清算的信號。
在此次拋售後，比特幣回升至$64,000關口，這是近兩週來首次收復該水平。
Bitwise研究主管Ryan Rasmussen表示，客戶仍在詢問Strategy是否構成集中風險，但大多數人認爲這已不再是比特幣的重大長期隱患。
下一個買家是「投資界的終極Boss」
Hougan表示，比特幣的歷史由一個主要買家將接力棒傳遞給下一個買家所定義：從密碼朋克到亞洲散戶投資者、美國散戶投資者、GBTC、Strategy，如今輪到了機構資本。
Hougan表示：「下一個邊際買家是投資界的終極Boss，那就是機構資本。」
Rasmussen表示，Vanguard正在尋找數字資產主管，這是傳統金融進一步進軍加密領域的又一跡象。
他表示，機構採用正在形成一股「浪潮」，隨着客戶和同行紛紛進入這一資產類別，資產管理公司、顧問、養老基金和捐贈基金越來越不得不考慮配置加密資產。
Hougan補充道，華爾街的職業風險已經逆轉。
早前，支持加密貨幣可能導致專業人士聲譽受損。他說，如今忽視數字資產反而可能帶來更大的風險。

translatedData.content:
#newt $NEWT Organization-level security isn’t a magic ticket—NEWT still has to prove that small transactions won’t be discouraged by cost
I work on payments products in Jakarta, and I’ve seen many “enterprise-grade security” features. They’re powerful and expensive. The problem is that ordinary users may not be willing to pay for that cost on every small transaction.
Newton’s pre-transaction screening is designed for high-value scenarios. RWA transfers, vault rebalancing, large stablecoin redemptions—these transactions deserve a full run of the policy, data checks, and proof process. But if users do just a one-off small action and go through the same heavy process, the cost and latency will become a turn-off.
This isn’t a question of whether the technology is advanced or not. It’s about how the security budget is allocated. A safe is for storing gold bars—not for opening it dozens of times every day to grab small change. If Newton wants to expand its use cases, it must design security tiers with different weights. Small transactions should use low-cost baseline checks, while large transactions use the full organization-level workflow.#ETH 
NEWT’s requirements also need this kind of layering to support them. If only high-value transactions use it, scale may grow slowly. If all small transactions get scared away by costs, the ecosystem won’t grow either. A truly good authorization layer should let users buy security according to risk—not force them to buy the highest tier every time.#BTC 
I’ll be watching the ongoing fee structure too. Per-transaction policy costs, whether failed transactions are charged, and whether small tasks have a lightweight mode—these are more practical than the words “organization-level security.”@NewtonProtocol

content:
#newt $NEWT 机构级安全不是万能门票，NEWT 还要证明小额交易不会被成本劝退
我在雅加达做支付产品，见过很多“企业级安全”功能。它们很强，也很贵。问题是，普通用户不一定愿意为每一笔小交易付这笔钱。
Newton 的交易前审查适合高价值场景。RWA 转让、vault 调仓、稳定币大额赎回，这些交易值得跑完整 policy、数据检查和证明流程。但如果用户只是做一笔小额操作，也走同样厚重的流程，成本和延迟就会变成劝退。
这不是技术先进不先进的问题，而是安全预算怎么分配。保险柜适合放金条，不适合每天开关几十次拿零钱。Newton 如果想扩大使用范围，必须设计轻重不同的安全档位。小额交易用低成本基础检查，大额交易用完整机构级流程。#ETH 
NEWT 的需求也要靠这个分层来支撑。如果只有高价值交易使用，规模可能慢；如果所有小额交易都被成本吓跑，生态也长不大。真正好的授权层，应该让用户按风险买安全，而不是被迫每次都买最高配。#BTC 
我会盯后续费用结构。单笔 policy 成本、失败交易是否收费、小额任务是否有轻量模式，这些比“机构级安全”几个字更现实。@NewtonProtocol

title: RWA 的拒绝权一旦上链，NEWT 要面对的就是法律和代码的双重账本
subTitle:
我在卢森堡帮基金管理人做过上链资产合规文件，最大的体会是：现实资产最麻烦的不是发行，而是拒绝。拒绝一个赎回，拒绝一个转让，拒绝一个地址进入白名单，拒绝一个投资人继续持有份额，每一次都要有理由，而且理由要经得起法律和账本同时追问。
RWA 上链以后，很多人只盯资产怎么映射，怎么托管，怎么交易，怎么提高流动性。但只要它牵涉现实权利，拒绝权就一定会出现。某个投资者不符合资格，某个地区临时受限，某笔资金来源被标记，某项资产触发合规审查。技术上交易可能能发出，法律上却不能放行。#Newt $NEWT 
Newton 的授权层如果进入 RWA 场景，就会碰到这道硬墙。它不能只说“policy 拒绝了”。这在普通 DeFi 里也许够用，在 RWA 里远远不够。因为 RWA 背后有合同、托管协议、基金章程、监管文件和客户权利。拒绝不是一个链上状态，而是一份可被追问的法律动作。
这就是我说的双重账本。第一本账本是代码账本，记录 policy hash、operator 签名、attestation、执行时间、数据源状态。第二本账本是法律账本，记录拒绝依据、适用条款、客户身份、司法辖区、申诉路径和责任主体。Newton 如果只处理第一本账本，还不够承接 RWA；如果能把两本账本的接口打通，它的价值才会变得很硬。
举个简单场景。某个 RWA vault 的份额持有人提交转让请求，链上地址没问题，资产余额也没问题，但接收方所在地区不符合发行文件约束。Newton 的 policy 拒绝交易。链上看，这只是一次 deny；现实里，这可能是一份法律通知的起点。用户会问：我被哪条规则拒绝？规则什么时候更新？我的状态数据是谁提供的？我能不能补材料？发行方是否有义务重新评估？
如果这些都靠人工客服补，链上授权层就没有真正闭环。Newton 更理想的做法，是让拒绝单本身携带足够的结构化证据：规则版本、适用条款引用、脱敏原因分类、数据源时间戳、负责方和后续路径。它不需要公开用户隐私，但必须让相关方知道拒绝不是拍脑袋。
NEWT 的商业机会也在这。RWA 不会为普通“安全感”付长期费用，但会为可审计、可追责、可出具记录的拒绝流程付费。现实金融里，拒绝文件、审批记录、审计轨迹都是成本。Newton 如果能把这些成本变成链上可验证服务，NEWT 才有更稳定的需求来源。#ETH 
但风险也同样大。代码和法律不总是同步。法律条款可能模糊，合规要求可能变化，不同司法辖区可能冲突。代码喜欢确定性，法律经常需要解释空间。一个 policy 写得太硬，可能误拒合法交易；写得太松，又可能放过高风险转让。RWA 的授权层不是纯技术问题，而是把法律不确定性压进代码边界里的工程。
我不认为 Newton 现在已经把这件事完全解决。它更像是在搭第一层轨道。未来真正的难点，是让律师、发行方、operator、数据源、链上合约和用户处在同一套证据格式里。否则链上证明再漂亮，现实争议一来，大家还是要回到邮件、PDF 和人工解释。#BTC 
所以我看 RWA 里的 NEWT，不会只看合作和资产规模。我会看拒绝记录是否可读，policy 是否能关联法律条款，申诉是否有路径，规则版本是否能追溯，数据源错误是否能纠正。RWA 的拒绝权一旦上链，它就不只是技术按钮，而是法律和代码一起盖章。
这枚章要是盖错了，谁都不能只说“系统判断”。@NewtonProtocol

translatedData.title: Once the right to refuse for RWA is put on-chain, NEWT will have to face the dual ledgers of law and code
translatedData.subTitle:
I helped asset managers in Luxembourg with blockchain compliance documentation for tokenized on-chain assets. The biggest lesson I learned is: the most troublesome part of real-world assets isn’t the issuance—it’s refusal. Refusing a redemption, refusing a transfer, refusing an address from entering a whitelist, refusing an investor to continue holding shares—each time you need a reason, and that reason must withstand scrutiny from both law and the ledger.
After RWA is put on-chain, many people focus only on how assets are mapped, how they are custodied, how they are traded, and how to improve liquidity. But the moment it involves real-world rights, the right to refuse will inevitably appear. A particular investor doesn’t meet the eligibility requirements, a certain region is temporarily restricted, a source of funds is flagged, an asset triggers a compliance review. Technically, the transaction may be sent, but legally it cannot be cleared.#Newt $NEWT

title: 如果 operator 也有“信用分”，NEWT 的下一层透明度才算开始
subTitle:
我在波兰做节点运维，最不信“去中心化网络里所有节点都一样”这句话。节点当然不一样。有人机器稳定，有人经常掉线；有人延迟低，有人证明提交慢；有人遇到异常会按规则处理，有人只想吃奖励；有人历史干净，有人早就该被社区盯上。#Newt 
Newton 现在谈 operator，更多还是从执行、签名、质押、惩罚这些角度讲。没错，这些是底层。但如果用户真的要把交易前审查、vault policy、AI agent 任务交给这套网络，光知道“有 operator 参与”还不够。用户应该知道：这次是谁在参与，它过去表现怎么样。$NEWT 
换句话说，operator 也需要信用分。
这个信用分不是传统金融那种黑箱评分，而是一套公开、可追踪、可解释的运行画像。比如在线率、平均响应延迟、P95 延迟、参与过多少次评估、是否出现过签名缺席、是否被 slash、是否在争议任务中站错边、是否经常处理高风险 policy、是否因为数据源异常导致过误拒。
这些信息如果不公开，operator 网络在用户眼里就是一群穿制服但不露脸的保安。你知道门口有人检查过你，却不知道他今天是不是睡着了，过去有没有放错人，手里的扫描仪是不是经常坏。
Newton 的 attestation 证明了某次任务有结果，但未来更重要的是证明结果背后的参与者值得信任。不是用一句“经济安全”概括，而是把 operator 的履历放出来。链上世界一直强调透明，但很多基础设施的透明只停在合约层，人的运行质量反而藏在后面。
NEWT 如果参与 operator 质押，它天然适合绑定这种声誉系统。质押金额只是第一层，不能代表全部安全。一个质押很多但经常延迟的 operator，不一定比一个质押较少但历史稳定的 operator 更适合执行高价值任务。未来 Newton 如果有任务分配市场，operator 信用分甚至应该影响任务优先级和可接任务类型。
比如低风险、小额、普通 policy 可以分给广泛 operator；高价值 vault、RWA 转让、稳定币大额赎回，就应该要求更高信誉、更高质押、更低延迟、更少历史争议的 operator 参与。这样安全不是一句统一口号，而是按任务风险分层。
当然，信用分本身也有风险。谁来设计评分？延迟和错误率会不会被操纵？新 operator 会不会永远拿不到高价值任务？大节点会不会因为历史数据积累形成垄断？这些问题都要提前想清楚。声誉系统一旦设计不好，会从透明工具变成准入门槛。
所以我更希望它是多维度公开面板，而不是单一分数。用户可以看到延迟、可用性、争议记录、参与任务类型和历史惩罚，而不是只看到一个神秘的 87 分。分数适合排序，明细才适合审计。#ETH 
我自己跑节点最怕的是网络只奖惩极端行为。作恶会被罚，正常执行有奖励，但中间大量“质量差但没犯规”的节点很难被识别。真实生产系统里，很多事故不是恶意，而是慢、乱、抖、没响应。operator 信用分正好可以填这个空白。
Newton 如果想成为交易前授权层，下一步透明度不该只停在 policy 和 attestation，而要延伸到 operator 运行质量。用户不只要知道交易被谁允许，还要知道允许它的人过去靠不靠谱。#BTC 
NEWT 的长期安全感，也许不是来自某个宏大口号，而是来自一张很朴素的节点成绩单。
@NewtonProtocol

translatedData.title: If operators also have a “credit score,” then Newton’s next layer of transparency truly begins
translatedData.subTitle:
I do node operations in Poland, and I don’t believe the phrase “in a decentralized network, all nodes are the same” at all. Of course nodes aren’t the same. Some machines are stable, some frequently drop offline; some have low latency, others have slow proof submissions; some handle exceptions according to the rules, others only want the rewards; some have a clean history, while others should have been flagged by the community long ago.#Newt 
When Newton talks about operators now, it’s still mostly from the angles of execution, signatures, staking, and penalties. Yes, those are the fundamentals. But if users really want to hand pre-transaction review, vault policy, and AI agent tasks to this network, it’s not enough just to know that “there are operators involved.” Users should know: who is participating this time, and how they performed in the past.$NEWT

translatedData.content:
#newt $NEWT Newton may not lack more policy, but rather a risk disclosure document ordinary people can understand
I worked on wallet products in Osaka, and I’m most afraid that after users see a bunch of security features, they become even more afraid. Not because the features are useless, but because they have no idea what they’re actually signing.
Newton now emphasizes policy, VaultKit, operator, and attestation—things that matter to developers and institutions. But ordinary users won’t read Rego, and they won’t understand the boundary conditions behind every rule. If you tell them “transactions are protected by policy,” they may only ask: Can I still transfer money? Will it get blocked? If something goes wrong, who do I contact? #ETH 
So Newton may not need more policy; what it needs is a risk disclosure document. #BTC 
This document doesn’t need to explain cryptography—just make five things clear: what this rule allows, what it forbids, what happens in the worst case, when it automatically expires, and how to handle it after a rejection. Users don’t need to understand the engine’s structure, but they must know which few “barriers” are protecting or restricting their funds.
If a security system only provides information that professionals can understand, it will stop at the institutional tooling stage. To reach a wider audience, Newton must translate the rules into plain language. Otherwise, the more policy there is, the more ordinary users will feel like they’re standing in front of a foreign-language contract and can only sign blindly.
NEWT’s long-term adoption depends not only on how strong the rules are written, but also on whether users can understand what exactly is protecting them while they use it. @NewtonProtocol

我在大阪做过钱包产品，最怕用户看到一堆安全功能后更害怕。不是因为功能没用，而是他们完全不知道自己签了什么。
Newton 现在强调 policy、VaultKit、operator、attestation，这些对开发者和机构很重要。但普通用户不会读 Rego，也不会理解每条规则背后的边界条件。你告诉他“交易受到 policy 保护”，他可能只会问：那我还能不能转钱？会不会被卡？出了事找谁？#ETH 
所以 Newton 也许不缺更多 policy，缺的是风险说明书。#BTC 
这份说明书不需要讲密码学，只要讲清五件事：这条规则允许什么，禁止什么，最坏情况下会发生什么，什么时候自动失效，被拒绝后怎么处理。用户不需要懂引擎结构，但必须知道自己的资金被哪几条栏杆围住。
安全系统如果只给专业用户看得懂，就会停在机构工具阶段。要走向更大范围，Newton 必须把规则翻译成人话。否则 policy 越多，普通用户越像站在外文合同前，只能盲签。
NEWT 的长期采用，不只取决于规则写得多强，也取决于用户能不能看懂自己正在被什么保护。@NewtonProtocol

title: Liquidity Is Rotating Into Bitcoin Before Altcoins Get Their Turn
subTitle:
Bitcoin just printed a 2.10 percent daily move to $62,999.63 while Ethereum barely managed 1.08 percent to $1,741.69. That gap is not noise. It is the fingerprint of capital rotating into the largest, most liquid crypto asset first — the same pattern that has preceded every meaningful altcoin cycle since 2020. The question is not whether alts follow. It is when, and how much of this move is real versus a head-fake in a market still negotiating with global macro headwinds.

Start with the tide. The Federal Reserve remains in a cautious posture. Rate cuts keep getting pushed out. The dollar index, despite recent softness, is not in freefall. Global liquidity is not gushing, but it is not contracting either — it is simmering. In that environment, smart money does not spread across ten thousand micro-caps. It concentrates. It goes to the asset with the deepest order book, the cleanest institutional rails, and the least execution risk. That asset is Bitcoin. The $1.05 billion in 24-hour Binance volume versus Ethereum's $318.35 million tells you exactly where the conviction sits right now.

This is the rotation thesis in real time. Capital enters through $BTC first because that is where the institutional plumbing connects — ETF flows, custody infrastructure, and the narrative primacy that makes Bitcoin the default risk-on proxy for the entire crypto complex. Only after Bitcoin establishes a range and volatility compresses do traders begin hunting for relative value in $ETH and the broader altcoin stack. Today's price action is stage one of that sequence.

Now look at the map. Bitcoin currently trades at $62,999.63, sitting between the 72-hour support at $61,544.56 and resistance at $64,700.00 according to Binance data. That support is the line buyers need to defend. If $61,544 holds on any retest, it confirms demand is absorbing profit-taking, and the range stays constructive for a push toward that $64,700 ceiling. Break above $64,700 with volume, and the rotation accelerates — that is the signal that triggers momentum into altcoins because it tells the market Bitcoin can sustain higher prices and the risk appetite is genuine. Conversely, if $61,544 gives way, the thesis weakens. A loss of that level would mean sellers are overpowering bids at the most-watched support of the week, and the capital rotation stalls before it starts. That is when alts bleed the hardest, because the liquidity tide that was supposed to lift everything suddenly recedes.

Ethereum, for its part, is a lagging indicator right now. At $1,741.69, it sits above its 72-hour support of $1,713.44 but well below resistance at $1,833.40. The spread between those levels is roughly 7 percent — a wide range that reflects indecision. Traders watching $ETH are essentially waiting for Bitcoin to make its move first. If BTC clears $64,700, expect Ethereum to test that $1,833 ceiling in sympathy. If Bitcoin loses $61,544, Ethereum's $1,713 support becomes the next battleground, and a breach there opens the door to deeper retests across the altcoin board.

The macro backdrop adds context. Sony Bank just secured US regulatory approval for stablecoin issuance — a signal that institutional infrastructure is being built regardless of short-term price noise. Hong Kong tightening anti-phishing measures suggests regulators are deepening engagement with crypto rather than retreating from it. These are liquidity-structure developments, not catalysts for a single candle, but they accumulate. They widen the institutional on-ramp that makes Bitcoin's dominance in capital rotation possible.

The regime read is straightforward. We are in an early risk-on rotation with Bitcoin leading. The Fed has not tipped hawkish. Liquidity is not contracting. But neither has the breakout happened yet — BTC is mid-range, and the setup is decided by whether $61,544 support holds or $64,700 resistance breaks. That makes the next few hours the cleanest window to position, because once the range resolves, the risk-reward compresses fast.

The $BTC pair on Binance is one tap away, and the levels above and below are where this whole rotation either accelerates or stalls. Defending support here or waiting for the break?

#newt $NEWT  Singapore’s downpour smashed against the window for the third hour. My quant buddy sent me a message: NEWT’s Season 2 point rules have changed again.

I stared at the screen and suddenly wanted to laugh. It’s not that the rules are changing—it's that the people in the comments are still doing the same old accounting with their last cycle’s logic: after TGE, how many days until unlock; whether you can farm Season points; whether locked staking APY can outperform.
They calculate it as “how to pull money out of the system,” but what NEWT is doing is precisely “how to make it so you can’t get as comfortable extracting it.”

In this space, that’s against common sense.

What’s the usual script? The project treats tokens like water—users show up, twist the faucet open right away, the metrics look beautiful, the community gets hyped—then everyone collectively collapses on the day the faucet is turned off. But at this stage, NEWT isn’t turning the faucet wider. It’s slowly closing it. Burn or Earn isn’t a benefit—it’s a math prison. You either burn points for short-term thrills, or lock them in and bet on long-term survival. It’s not trying to please you; it’s filtering you: are you the leftover fuel for arbitrage, or a digital tenant willing to be locked inside this system? #BTC #ETH 

A lot of people call this a “trap”—a “locked-staking trap.” But if you calm down and look closely, it’s the first time it has shifted the design perspective from “how to let early players break even in three months” to “whether this system will still exist next year.” The difference in between is a rebuild of the survival logic.

NEWT now has no gray area. It’s not that kind of air coin propped up by KOL calls and Twitter sentiment. It’s fully welded into this governance model. No matter how fancy the MPC terminal looks, and no matter how loudly the cross-chain aggregation is hyped—if Burn or Earn doesn’t involve real consumption, and if Season points are just another round of point-farming frenzy, once you lay the on-chain data out flat, it’s all naked swimming.

So don’t obsess over the chart. Watch something more fundamental: whether NEWT’s “lock-up + governance transition + point burn” triangular architecture has started being copied by other projects.

If next month you don’t see another pipeline project chanting “minting tokens is the peak,” but instead you see many of them slowing down, locking up, and compressing arbitrage space into thin slices—then this won’t be about whether a coin goes up or down anymore.
That will be the whole sector finally switching from “how to hand out money” to “how to collect taxes and keep surviving.”

That—really—is a paradigm shift. Not a celebration, but the quiet consolidation of class. @NewtonProtocol

#newt $NEWT 新加坡暴雨砸在窗上的第三个小时，我那做量化的哥们儿发来一条消息：NEWT的Season 2积分规则又改了。

我盯着屏幕，突然想笑。不是规则在变，是评论区那帮人——还在用上一轮脑回路算账：TGE后几天解锁、Season积分能不能刷、锁仓APY能不能跑赢。他们算"怎么从系统里抽钱"，但NEWT干的事，恰恰是"怎么让你抽得没那么舒服"。

这在这个赛道里，是反常识的。

正常剧本是什么？项目方把代币当水，用户一来就拧开水龙头，数据做漂亮了，社区嗨了，然后等水龙头拧干的那天集体崩盘。但NEWT走到现在，水龙头不是拧大了，是在慢慢关小。Burn or Earn不是福利，是数学监牢——你要么把积分烧了换短期爽感，要么锁进去赌长期存活。它不是在讨好你，它在筛选你：你是来套利的燃料残渣，还是愿意被锁进这个系统的数字佃农？#BTC #ETH 

很多人骂这是"套"，是"锁仓陷阱"。但你冷静下来看，它第一次把设计视角从"怎么让早期玩家三个月回本"切换到了"这个系统明年还在不在"。这中间的差别，是生存逻辑的重构。

NEWT现在没有暧昧地带。它不是那种靠KOL喊单、靠推特情绪能撑住的空气币，它是完全焊死在这套治理模型上的。MPC终端做得再花哨，跨链聚合吹得再响，如果Burn or Earn没有真实消耗，如果Season积分只是又一场刷分狂欢，那链上数据一摊开，全是裸泳。

所以别盯K线，盯一件更底层的事：NEWT这套"锁仓+治理过渡+积分销毁"的三角架构，有没有开始被其他项目抄作业。

如果下个月开始，你看到的不是又一个"发币即巅峰"的流水线项目，而是纷纷跟着降速、跟着锁、跟着把套利空间压成刀片——那NEWT就不是一个币的涨跌问题了。那是整个赛道终于从"怎么发钱"切换到了"怎么活着收税"。

那才是真正的范式转移。不是狂欢，是静默的阶级固化。@NewtonProtocol

#newt $NEWT Friday 2 a.m. in a tiny Shinjuku apartment in Tokyo—less than twenty square meters—I stare at the intent execution panel on Newton.xyz. Beside me is my third cup of black coffee gone cold.

Originally, I just wanted to casually stake a bit of NEWT and let an AI agent run a few cross-chain intents, just to make things convenient. TEE, ZKP, automation—doesn’t that basically amount to giving DeFi an autopilot?

I follow old Deg’s playbook: manually calculate APY, watch the unlock curve, compare it against the 14-day cooling period, trying to squeeze every last drop of capital efficiency.

After running two days of testnet, I feel colder and colder—not because the air-conditioning is too high, but because I realize I’m effectively doing the protocol’s “human verification” for free.

You think automation is working for you? No—it’s you who provides “credibility” for the automation.

While running intents, I scroll Kaito’s yappers leaderboard. None of the top ones are talking about APY. They’re breaking down the compliance architecture of the Keystore rollup, mapping how GENIUS Act translates onto-chain, and arguing why Newton can become an “institutional compliance channel” for firms to enter.

The ecosystem’s 15.5% reserves are thrown at the yappers—not to let you be a staking miner, but to have you act as a “technical missionary.”

This is the most covert selection mechanism of NEWT: it seems to recruit automation users on the surface, but what it actually recruits are “narrative contractors” who can translate the black box into Wall Street language.

Many people are still calculating the 14.85% compounding rate, how the 14-day cooling period can be hedged. But have you considered that the small amount of coins you earn by locking for three months might be worth less than the compliance-thread value VC forwards?

I changed my whole strategy. No more chasing TVL—I’m chasing “the right to interpret.” #ETH 

The intents still run as usual, but every failed revert, every cross-chain delay, every TEE proof generation time—I archive it all. In this arena, “having stepped on the pitfalls” is itself the rarest narrative fuel.

Infrastructure protocols never reward the first wave of users. They reward the people who can turn the “usage process” into “cognitive assets.”

Whoever gets “Newton = the on-chain entry point for institutional compliance” into the subconscious of traditional finance professionals will be the one who scoops up the biggest pour from the 15.5% incentive pool.

So stop being that automation tester still tweaking the gas limit at 2 a.m.

In this round, the most valuable thing was never that 14.85% staking yield.

It’s the exclusive right to define what “on-chain compliance” really means. #NEWT@NewtonProtocol

📰 Crypto Market Hotspot Dispatch

1. Ethereum Foundation: AI is strong at finding vulnerabilities by “making hypotheses,” but hard at “verifying what’s real”
A recent technical article from the Ethereum Foundation points out that the core bottleneck of using AI to assist security research is not discovering suspicious issues, but proving that a vulnerability is genuinely real and reproducible in production code. The protocol security team said that collaborative AI agents have already found real defects in relevant dependency systems, but a significant amount of time is still spent filtering out false positives. A more practical path now is to position AI as a research assistant—conducting phased reviews with multiple agents, gradually narrowing the attack surface, and improving report credibility and verification efficiency.

2. The U.S. “CLEAR Act” moves into a critical stage; a digital-asset regulatory framework may see new progress
Senate negotiations on the “CLEAR Act” are entering the final window. Recent developments show that the relevant parties are preparing to submit a consolidated legislative draft, integrating the versions from the Banking and Agriculture Committees into a single text. The added content is expected to be substantial, with an emphasis leaning more toward consumer protection. The bill aims to establish a federal-level regulatory framework for the digital asset market and further clarify the boundary of authority between the SEC and the CFTC. However, bipartisan consensus has not yet fully formed, so the outcome of subsequent talks remains a key focus for the market.

3. SpaceX launches coverage with Wall Street analysts; market sentiment is somewhat optimistic
After the relevant quiet period ended, Wall Street analysts have begun formally publishing research views on SpaceX. In the latest coverage, some institutions have offered relatively positive assessments, with the logic largely based on SpaceX’s leading position in commercial space, and the expectation that its advantages may expand further after competitors adjust their strategies. While this is not a direct event for the crypto industry, Musk-related assets and market sentiment have often had strong spillover effects; in the short term, they may continue to influence risk appetite for technology, aerospace, and certain concept tokens.

4. Hyperliquid and Phantom jointly urge the CFTC to define on-chain infrastructure regulatory boundaries
Hyperliquid’s policy center and Phantom recently submitted a joint comment to the U.S. CFTC, urging a clear distinction between the roles of “infrastructure developers” and “regulated financial service providers.” Key points include: confirming that simply publishing on-chain protocol software itself should not be regarded as an activity requiring registration; providing a compliance path for licensed exchanges and clearing institutions to use on-chain infrastructure; and further formalizing the concept of regulatory exemptions related to non-custodial wallets. This move reflects the industry’s proactive push to secure a clearer and more predictable regulatory framework for on-chain infrastructure.
